chunks: Salih ibn Uqba from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Ju'fi said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, loves the one who engages in playful banter within the group without obscenity.

key_terms.الْمُدَاعِبَ: The one who engages in playful banter or humor

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on humor and banter in social gatherings?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the permissibility and spiritual merit of social levity, provided it remains free from rafath (obscenity or indecency). It reflects the Shia emphasis on balancing seriousness with joy, fostering communal harmony through permissible amusement that pleases Allah.

en.hubeali: Salih Bin Uqba, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Ju’fy who said,
‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Loves the humour (taking place) in the group without there being any obscenities’.
en.sarwar: 4. Salih ibn ‘Aqabah has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Ju’fi who has said the following: “
I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, loves a funny storyteller in a group free of abusive matters. ’”
